key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that approximately 0.5% biaxial tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic at 300 K while retaining preferential molecular orientations.
engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial design of perovskite absorbers by predicting phase stability and band-gap shifts that static calculations miss.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond bulk and free-standing slab simulations with constrained in-plane lattice vectors.
Track lattice ratios, octahedral tilts, molecular orientations, and snapshot-averaged band gaps.
evidence_signal: The predicted transition agrees with experiments on MAPbI₃ films on KCl, bulk and slab trends are consistent, and snapshot-averaged band gaps reproduce the experimental tensile-strain blue shift.
watch_item: Free-standing slabs do not explicitly capture substrate-interface chemistry, which may affect transferability to specific epitaxial systems.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
